name: Backdooms
tagline: DOOM in the Backrooms, in a GIF. No install, no server.
description:
It is one file. Open it and you are in the yellow halls — nothing to install, no account, no server, and it runs with the wifi off. Your best run is saved inside the file itself, so the GIF you hand someone is the game and your score together.

The halls are real. Wallpaper with a chair rail and a skirting board that run away to a vanishing point, ceiling tiles you can count, a line of fluorescents marching off into the dark, damp carpet with a pool of light under each one. Things the colour of dried blood come down the corridor at you, and you hear them before the lights find them. The shotgun is a pump — seven pellets, a kick, and a flash that lights the hall.

WASD and the mouse on a computer; Esc hands the pointer back, click to take it again. On a phone the left thumb is a stick that appears wherever you put it, the rest of the screen looks, and FIRE keeps firing while you hold it.

Send the invite and whoever opens the link wakes in the same maze, from the same seed, and shows up down the corridor as a pale figure. You can watch them walk. You can shoot them. There is no game server and no lobby — the room is the link.

An unofficial port of Backdooms by Kuber Mehta, itself inspired by DOOM (1993) and The Backrooms. The original fits inside a QR code, which is the entire point of it; this one spends the room a GIF has on the things a QR code could never afford — textured walls, a floor and a ceiling, monsters with a silhouette, sound with nothing to download, a save, and other people.
